findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket are stored unencrypted by default (relying solely on SSE-S3 default which is not explicitly enforced, and no bucket policy denies unencrypted uploads). Sensitive report data could be stored without encryption guarantees.

findings.issue_category: no access control / public exposure risk
findings.description: No 'acl' attribute is set and no public access block is configured, leaving the bucket subject to default ACL behavior and without explicit protection against public access misconfiguration.

This bucket stores financial ledger export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, meaning sensitive financial data is not encrypted at rest by a customer-managed or explicit policy.
The bucket has versioning and logging configured but no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving model artifacts unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket containing operational runbooks, risking exposure of sensitive operational data if accessed improperly.

The bucket uses the 'log-delivery-write' canned ACL which grants write and read-ACP permissions to the S3 log delivery group; combined with force_destroy and no public access block, this could allow unintended access if not tightly scoped.

The object is uploaded to reports_archive, a bucket without server-side encryption configured, and the object itself does not specify server_side_encryption, so the vendor roster file (potentially sensitive) is stored without encryption at rest.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be destroyed without recovery, which combined with lack of versioning increases risk of irrecoverable data loss if an attacker or erroneous process triggers deletion.
